candidates.heuristic_context: Target problem types: heterogeneous cases processed in a uniform way, so simple cases carry the effort of complex ones. Applicable when cases with clearly different recorded characteristics all follow the same path.
candidates.additional_context: case:Product = 'A' splits the log into 278 and 2722 cases that are routed differently at 2 gateway(s), reaching 2 activities: 'diagnosis 2nd', 'replace'. The mined model has no access to the attribute, so each of those gateways uses one pooled probability for every case — strongest example, case:Product = 'A' reaches 'diagnosis 2nd' 100% of the time against 0% for the rest (z=54.8), while the model sends 11% of arrivals there regardless. The redesign attaches the condition at every one of those gateways, so the case type is routed consistently rather than at a coin flip. ⚠️ The condition is a HARD predicate, so it sends 100% of this type to 'diagnosis 2nd' and 0% of the rest, where the log shows 100% and 0% — 0 percentage points of standardisation beyond what the log already does, which is the intervention rather than a reproduction of it. ⚠️ This changes WHICH cases go where, not how long anything takes: no hours are assumed anywhere, and whether routing by type helps, hurts or does nothing is for the simulation to measure. ⚠️ Direction of the change: in the log a case that reaches 'diagnosis 2nd' still records 1.7 further events and 37.555 h of further work, against 4.2 events and 86.043 h for an average case. Part of the case still lies ahead of it, so the rule shifts work rather than plainly adding or removing it.
